name: Congenital Subglottic Stenosis

criteria.description: Endoscopic visualization of subglottic airway narrowing present at birth
Presence of biphasic stridor and respiratory distress in neonate or infant
Imaging evidence (CT or MRI) of subglottic airway narrowing without acquired cause
Exclusion of acquired causes such as trauma, infection, or prolonged intubation

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of endoscopic confirmation of congenital subglottic narrowing with characteristic clinical respiratory symptoms and exclusion of acquired causes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis relies heavily on endoscopic evaluation and clinical presentation in early infancy.

pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic noisy breathing during both inspiration and expiration

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital subglottic airway narrowing confirmed by endoscopy
searchTerms: narrowed airway below vocal cords from birth

common.symptomName: Respiratory distress in neonate or infant
searchTerms: breathing difficulty in newborn or infant
bluish skin during feeding or upset
turning blue when crying or eating

common.symptomName: Stridor exacerbated by crying or exertion
searchTerms: high-pitched noisy breathing worsened by crying

occasional.symptomName: Feeding difficulties due to airway obstruction
searchTerms: feeding problems due to blocked airway
poor feeding caused by airway issues

occasional.symptomName: Failure to thrive secondary to chronic respiratory compromise
searchTerms: poor growth from chronic breathing problems
failure to thrive due to respiratory issues

rare.symptomName: Pulmonary hypertension secondary to chronic hypoxia
searchTerms: lung artery hypertension from low oxygen
pulmonary hypertension due to chronic hypoxia

rare.symptomName: Stridor worsening with upper respiratory tract infections
searchTerms: stridor worsens with colds or infections
breathing noise increases with respiratory infections

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; no specific laboratory markers
imaging: CT or MRI showing subglottic airway narrowing
Chest X-ray may show hyperinflation or atelectasis secondary to airway obstruction
genetic: No specific genetic mutation identified; usually sporadic
other: Direct laryngotracheoscopy is gold standard for diagnosis
Pulmonary function tests may show fixed upper airway obstruction pattern in older children

distinguishingFeatures: History of prolonged intubation or airway trauma
Inflammatory or fibrotic changes on endoscopy
No fixed subglottic narrowing on endoscopy
Compression of trachea by vascular anomaly

redFlags: Failure to thrive due to chronic airway obstruction
references: Cotton RT. Congenital subglottic stenosis. In: Cummings Otolaryngology - Head and Neck Surgery. 7th ed. 2015.
